page: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro system. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz using the x86_64 architecture. The instance configuration provides 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled, operating under a burstable CPU allocation model. System memory consists of 4.0 GB of DDR5 running at 7 GHz, yielding an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is not included, as GPU count is zero. There is no bundled local storage, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-thread execution driven by high clock speeds and modern instruction set architectures, including AVX-512 and AMX extensions. In single-threaded tasks, the instance achieved 2164.0 in Geekbench single-core tests, 34.07 GB/sec in gzip compression, and 14.14 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, all ranking in the upper quartile of evaluated systems. Conversely, aggregate parallel throughput is constrained by the 2-vCPU ceiling and burstable execution model, reflected in a multi-core Geekbench score of 2700.0 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 2164.08. Memory bandwidth for large uncached reads reached 20.61 GB/sec, aligning with entry-tier memory throughput.

Given its hardware proportions and burstable CPU profile, c8i-flex.large offers an efficient compute footprint for applications with intermittent compute demands. Tradeoffs center on the absence of dedicated local disks and baseline network capacity, limiting sustained I/O-heavy operations. The instance is suited for batch processing, lightweight web serving, single-threaded utility tasks, compilation routines, and continuous integration runners that benefit from modern Intel CPU instructions without requiring continuous multi-core saturation.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.large is an entry-tier compute-optimized instance based on the Nitro hypervisor and x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C architecture running at 3.9 GHz. It features 2 burstable vCPUs across 1 physical core, 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz, zero GPUs, and no bundled local storage. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 2164.0 and 34.07 GB/sec in gzip compression. However, multi-core capacity and uncached memory throughput are structurally restricted by the single-core topology and burstable resource allocation. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this configuration provides a balanced footprint for bursty single-threaded workloads, lightweight microservices, and CI/CD tasks.
